neighbours.label: ' real' / ' finite' / ' complex' as mathematical qualifiers of numbers, fields and variances
fire: Let x be any real number strictly greater than zero.
The estimator is consistent provided the errors have finite variance.
Every polynomial factors completely over the field of complex numbers.
Multiply each entry of the matrix by a real scalar c.
A vector space over a finite field has only finitely many elements.
The roots of this equation are real and distinct when the discriminant is positive.
Assume the random variable has a finite mean and a finite second moment.
Each eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix is a real number.
quiet: Let x be any whole number strictly greater than zero.
The estimator is consistent provided the errors are independent.
Every polynomial factors completely over a suitable extension.
Multiply each entry of the matrix by a constant c.
A vector space over this field has a basis of three elements.
The roots of this equation are distinct when the discriminant is positive.
Assume the random variable has a known mean and a known second moment.
Each eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix is a positive number.
